newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says plans to proceed with Zaire mission.
newsitem.headline: Canada says plans to proceed with Zaire mission.

text.p: Canada has had enough positive responses to proceed with the initial steps of an international humanitarian mission for eastern Zaire, Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Thursday.

He told reporters that 15 countries, including the United States, had agreed to participate in the plan, which involved setting up a military headquarters in Uganda and working on a plan to airdrop relief supplies into eastern Zaire.
Axworthy said he would be calling a meeting on Friday of a steering board or contact group, which would be necessary to give final confirmation for the mission.
"There's still an ongoing tragedy," he said of the crisis in the region.
Earlier on Thursday, Zaire rejected a Canadian plan to airdrop food for thousands of refugees and Zairians fighting in the east of the country.
"The Zairian government is categorically opposed to the Canadian proposition to drop foodstuffs for refugees and displaced Zairians," Information Minister Boguo Makeli said.
